transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well... I guess I'm here because I just feel really restless. Like I can't settle in my own body anymore. It's... it's mostly when I'm supposed to sit quietly and do things like paperwork or figure out household plans. I just... can't.
When did you first start noticing this restlessness? Has it always been this way, or is this something new that started recently?

Um... I'm not really sure if it's completely new. But... it's definitely been noticeably worse for about a year and five months. Since I got married. I guess... when our routines merged, it just became a lot harder to ignore.
When you feel this restlessness, do you find yourself needing to move around, fidget, or do things with your hands and body? Or is it more of an internal feeling of not being able to relax?

Um... it's physical, I guess. I move. 

Like... if we're at church, or sitting down for a family dinner... I'm usually twisting my wedding ring around. Or my foot is bouncing. I try really hard to just... sit still and look normal, but I end up shifting around in my chair a lot anyway.

Going back further — when you were a child in school, did you have similar difficulties sitting still and paying attention in class, or is this fidgeting and restlessness something that's really only started happening in the past year or two?

Um... I guess it's not exactly new. 

Looking back... it was there when I was a kid. Elementary school. I was... well, my desk was always a mess. I'd forget permission slips. And... teachers would send notes home. Saying I talked out of turn, or... couldn't stay in my seat. So, yeah. I guess it's been a while.

When you're trying to focus on something that requires concentration — like reading, working on a project, or following along in a conversation — do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you get distracted easily?

Um... yeah, it's hard. 

I try to focus. Like... if I sit down to read an email about planning something, or even just a chapter in a book... I start out okay. But then... maybe a few minutes later, I'm just staring at the same paragraph. And I realize I didn't actually take any of it in.
Do you find yourself acting without thinking things through first — like interrupting people, making quick decisions you later regret, or doing things impulsively?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. 

I try really hard to be polite. But... if my husband is talking to someone, I might just... jump in. Or if someone is talking, I end up finishing their sentence. It's not that I want to be rude, it just... comes out. Before I can stop myself.

Beyond the fidgeting and attention issues you've mentioned, do you struggle with things like organizing your time, planning ahead, keeping track of deadlines, or getting started on tasks — even things you want to do?

Um... I don't really know. 

I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean... I manage okay, mostly. I don't really keep track of things in a specific way. I just sort of... get through the day.

When things don't go the way you expected, or if someone criticizes you, how do you typically react emotionally? Do you find yourself getting frustrated or upset more easily than you think other people do?

Um... I don't really think so. 

I mean... nobody likes being criticized, I guess. But... I don't think I get more upset than anyone else would. If things don't work out, it's frustrating, but... I just try to move on. I don't really let it get to me that much.

How much do these difficulties with focus, fidgeting, and interrupting actually affect your daily life — like your work, your marriage, or your relationships with family and friends? Would you say they cause you real problems, or are you managing okay overall?

Um... I guess it causes some issues. 

I mean... at home, and with the volunteering I do... people can't really count on me. Not reliably, anyway. I try really hard, but... I just keep letting things fall through. So... I've had to step back from some of my responsibilities lately. 

I just... yeah. I guess it's been a little difficult.

When you were younger, or even now — did teachers or family members ever say you talked too much, or that you seemed to have a lot of energy and had trouble staying still? Like, did you get in trouble for running around or being too active?

Um... I guess so, yeah. 

I mean, even back in elementary school, it was kind of like this. I was always the one with the really messy desk. And I'd forget to bring in permission slips... things like that. 

My parents used to get notes from my teachers. They'd say I was talking out of turn, or... that I couldn't stay in my seat. So... yeah, I guess it's been around for a while.
